OCD is an incredibly painful illness. It's actually NOT a mental illness. It's a neurological condition caused by inflammation and damage to specific regions of the brain (It's on the same spectrum as Tourette's and 1/3 or so of people have symptoms from both categories... like me). The portions of your brain that actually control the way your brain processes fear are completely screwed up in a person with OCD. In a huge number of people it starts after an infection around the age of five. There are genetic predispositions some people have that make them more likely to have this sort of immune reaction when they are young.

I couldn't hug my family members without have to shower afterwards. I couldn't shake people's hands, and my mind was racked 24/7 by lists I couldn't stop making. I would wash my hands with bleach and ammonia to the point I had sores on my hands.

It's really not a funny illness and it actually has nothing to do with "wanting to keep your desk straightened" or "going back to check the lights a second time" on your way out the door.

When I was diagnosed it was taking about 8 hours of my day away. Only a small percentage of people respond to SSRI treatments. Realistically they are ineffective.
